clue.text: Approach clear river

blocks.note: overt means open, clear to see
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A walker is told to approach the bank and cross the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening move or offer made to someone, a synonym of approach as a noun.

clue.text: Plump spies breaking in, looking professional?

indicators.note: spies breaking into somewhere end up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
the word in itself, opening around the spies
the American intelligence agency
the rest of the word in, closing around the spies

explanation.surface: Overweight spies break into a building, trying to look like professionals.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' does double duty: it signals the breaking-in and also supplies the letters the spies sit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician's profession is the eyes and eyesight, so the question mark makes a playful definition of someone whose job is looking.

clue.text: Silent actor's bonus

blocks.note: first meaning: a film player with no lines who fills out a crowd scene
second meaning: something additional, over and above what is due

explanation.surface: A non-speaking film performer receives a bonus payment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a non-speaking background performer and an additional item, so both halves of the clue fit.

clue.text: Call from Hunt to agree with House

blocks.note: figures that tally agree with each other
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A politician named Hunt calls on the House of Commons to agree.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital H on Hunt suggests a politician; here it is a fox hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the cry huntsmen give on sighting a fox, so it is literally a call heard from a hunt.

clue.text: Sell out, absorbing current quota

indicators.note: whatever absorbs something takes it in, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: to rat on someone is to betray them, sell them out
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A trader sells out, taking up the current allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allowance or share, the same idea as a quota.

clue.text: Band claiming place in big story

indicators.note: a thing claiming something takes hold of it, wrapping it inside

blocks.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the body
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A pop band claims a place in a major news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a prominently displayed front-page news story, a big story in newspaper slang.

clue.text: Award gold for lack of improvement?

blocks.note: a plate is a trophy, a prize in racing
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Giving someone a gold medal for failing to improve.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a stage where progress levels off, so it describes a period without improvement; the question mark flags the figurative sense.

clue.text: Estranged cadet, a 'Neil Armstrong', returned for a bit

indicators.note: only a bit of the phrase is used, a run of letters sitting across the words
something returned goes back the way it came, so read the letters from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of cadet to the start of Armstrong

explanation.surface: A cadet who styles himself the next Neil Armstrong is estranged from his crew after returning.
explanation.walkthrough: The run DET A NEIL A, read backwards, gives ALIENATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienated means made unfriendly or distant from someone, the sense of estranged.

clue.text: Minimal settlement for lead in drama

blocks.note: first meaning: a very small village
second meaning: the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy about the Prince of Denmark

explanation.surface: A small settlement payment is made for a leading actor in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a tiny village without a church and the Danish prince who is the lead role of Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Contemptuous sporting authority involved in lying

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

blocks.note: the Football Association, English football's governing body
prone means lying face down

explanation.surface: A contemptuous sports body is caught up in lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane means showing irreverence or disrespect for sacred things, akin to contemptuous.

clue.text: Tyranny of a tsar not working with militia

indicators.note: the letters are put to work and remade into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The tyranny of a tsar who is out of work but still has a militia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' reads as one phrase, but 'not' is part of the fodder and only 'working' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalitarianism is a system of absolute centralised state control, a form of tyranny.

clue.text: Shout about extreme characters flipping switch in game

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round another
flipping something turns it over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to cry is to shout
A and Z are the letters at either end of the alphabet
to switch is to whip with a thin stick, to flog

explanation.surface: Someone shouts about a few odd characters flicking a switch during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a light switch; here it is a verb, to beat with a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy golf is a novelty miniature putting game with obstacles, so it is a game.

clue.text: Wise knight entering lake

indicators.note: a thing entering another goes inside it

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
Lake Erie, one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A wise knight wades into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' looks like an adjective for the knight, but it is the surname of Ernie Wise, of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian Ernie Wise is identified by surname alone, so the first name answers the surname clue.

clue.text: Order in official document about author

indicators.note: one item sits in the other, held inside it
turned about, the combined letters face the other way

blocks.note: the first letter of visa, the travel document, which wraps round the order
the Order of Merit, a British honour
the rest of visa

explanation.surface: An instruction written in an official document concerns a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: OM goes inside VISA as V-OM-ISA, and the whole is then turned round to give ASIMOV.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was the prolific science-fiction writer of I, Robot, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: Noticing flying object, initially unidentified

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order
initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of object

explanation.surface: Someone notices a flying object which at first cannot be identified: a UFO.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying object' reads as a UFO, but 'flying' stirs up the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incognito has concealed their identity, so they go about unidentified.

clue.text: Bathroom units replaced in midweek?

indicators.note: items replaced are put back differently, so the letters are rearranged
one part goes in the other, sitting inside it

blocks.note: the first of the two middle letters of week
the letters of units rearranged
the second of the two middle letters of week

explanation.surface: Bathroom fittings are swapped out in the middle of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-week is EE, the centre of week, which wraps round the jumbled units.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a bathroom attached directly to a bedroom, as in hotel rooms.

clue.text: Head of AC-12 arresting Detective Sergeant etc

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
police arresting someone take them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the first letter of AC
twelve o'clock is noon
the standard abbreviation for the police rank

explanation.surface: The boss of AC-12, the anti-corruption unit in the TV drama Line of Duty, arrests a detective sergeant and others.
explanation.walkthrough: AC-12 looks like one name from Line of Duty, but splits into AC and the number twelve, read as a time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: And so on is the spoken phrase that etc abbreviates, short for et cetera.

clue.text: Charity resettled majority of grey seals

indicators.note: the majority is most but not all, so the word loses its final letter
things resettled are moved into a new arrangement

blocks.note: most of grey, its last letter dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A charity relocates most of a colony of grey seals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority of' looks like it applies to the seals, but it trims only grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or gifts, close to charity in the sense of benevolence.

clue.text: Music-maker's raincoat shortly getting tailored

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its last letter
tailoring cuts and reshapes material, so the letters are refashioned

blocks.note: raincoat with its final letter cut

explanation.surface: A musician's raincoat is taken in to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the music-maker has the trimmed raincoat rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, something that makes music.

clue.text: Did gag take lead from broken-hearted?

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: wretched means miserable, heartbroken

explanation.surface: A comic wonders whether his joke took its lead from someone heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke but is a verb, to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave as if vomiting, which is what gagging is, both in the past tense.

clue.text: Religious figure's friend had converted

indicators.note: something converted is changed into another form, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: bud is American slang for a pal
the letters of had rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious leader's friend had been converted to the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' reads as religious conversion, but it reorders only had.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddha is the title of Siddhartha Gautama, founder of Buddhism, a central figure of that religion.

clue.text: Monkeys feature in limitless curse

indicators.note: the feature is placed in the other piece, sitting inside it
without limits means losing the letters at both ends

blocks.note: the opening of curse once its outer letters go
the chin is a facial feature
the rest of curse without its last letter

explanation.surface: Monkeys appear in an endless curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Curse loses its outer letters, leaving URS, around CHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkeys is an informal name for mischievous children, the same sense as urchins.

clue.text: Almost register to secure popular health centre

indicators.note: almost all of the word is kept, its last letter falling away
to secure something is to hold it fast inside

blocks.note: when something clicks it registers or sinks in
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Almost signing up to secure a well-liked health centre.
explanation.walkthrough: CLICK loses its last letter to give CLIC, which holds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a place where patients go for medical treatment, a health centre.

clue.text: Rough journey for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is judged by sound

blocks.note: a course is a route or journey, said the same as its rough-textured twin

explanation.surface: Accountants' auditors face a rough trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditors look like accountants checking books, but here they are hearers.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough in texture or manner, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Allowed to take flight

blocks.note: first meaning: lawful, permitted, informally
second meaning: as two words, to run away

explanation.surface: Permission to board a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is slang for legitimate, permitted; split as leg it it is British slang for running off quickly.

clue.text: Put lid on e.g. German snack

blocks.note: to scotch a plan is to put an end to it
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Putting a lid on a German dish, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a British picnic snack: a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg is a hard-boiled egg in a sausage-meat coating, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Medical procedure involved in gene mapping

indicators.note: the letters are involved within the words, running across the gap

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A medical procedure involved in genetic mapping research.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is the medical injection of fluid into the rectum, a procedure.

clue.text: Soap opera embracing script's cordiality

indicators.note: something embracing another wraps its arms around it

blocks.note: Neighbours is a long-running Australian TV soap
an actor's lines are their script

explanation.surface: A soap opera's script is full of warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbourliness is friendly, helpful warmth toward those around you, a close synonym of cordiality.

clue.text: Outskirts of city restricting bright grey?

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept
restricting means hemming in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: the first edge letter of city
loud colours are bright, garish ones
the other edge letter of city

explanation.surface: City suburbs are hemming in brightness, leaving everything grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' seems the opposite of the answer, yet loud colours are bright ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudy sky is overcast and grey, so grey with a question mark describes weather by example.

clue.text: Convince Edward, a US representative, to make a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Ed is the short form of Edward
taken as written
taken as written
rep is short for representative

explanation.surface: Persuading Edward, an American congressman, to return to politics.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone is to talk them into believing or doing something, the same as convince.
